Subject: Post-call: actionable SLA models & warm-pool design for Acuity Health

Thanks again for the call earlier — good discussion and helpful context. To keep momentum, I wanted to capture a concise set of performance targets and a couple of alternative warm-pool/autoscale designs so we can converge on a PoC scope.

Summary of asks from our side (what we heard):
- Target user-facing latency: p95 <= 350 ms (streaming allowed with first-token <= 120 ms and steady token latency target <= 15 ms).
- Concurrency/throughput: steady baseline ~200 RPS, expected spikes up to ~800 RPS for 2–5 minute bursts; occasional multi-hour peaks up to 1,200 concurrent requests during campaigns.
- Streaming: ~30% of calls will use streaming (partial tokens + mid-stream cancellations).
- Reliability: 99.9% regional availability target with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model or degraded rate rather than hard errors).
- Queueing tolerance: sub-5s queueing acceptable for autoscale windows; prefer smooth latency for streaming.

Questions we still need from you (to finalize the sizing/maths):
1) Confirm the exact percent of traffic that must hit full-fidelity model vs acceptable fallback.
2) Confirm spike profile: how often per week/month do the 800+ RPS spikes occur, and typical duration distribution.
3) Any regulatory/retention constraints that affect caching or KV reuse.

Attached is a starter SLA model (SLA-models-v1.pdf) and a short example traffic sample we discussed. If you can return a CSV with a 24–72 hour request-level sample (timestamps + avg token length + streaming flag), Ben will run a sizing run and propose a warm-pool config (GPU counts prewarmed, per-GPU concurrency, expected scale-up timeline).

Proposed next steps:
- You: share sample traffic export (CSV) and confirm fallback acceptance percentage — target by Wed 10/21.
- Us: deliver two concrete warm-pool designs + cost/latency tradeoffs by Fri 10/23.
- Schedule: 60-min technical deep-dive to validate assumptions — propose Thu 10/22 or Mon 10/26.

Thanks —

Tessa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the numbers from our side and adding a couple clarifications:

- Fidelity mix: ~85% of requests must use full-fidelity model. The remaining ~15% can be routed to a smaller fall-back model during extreme overload.
- Spike cadence: expected 800–1,000 RPS spikes usually 1–2x/week tied to marketing pushes; we had a 1,200 RPS event last quarter that lasted ~12 minutes.
- Streaming: yes ~30% of calls streaming; most streaming calls are short (5–15 tokens after the initial prompt).
- Data retention/regulatory: logs retained for 90 days; no special KV residency needs but PII must be redacted before being sent to vendor logs.

I attached a 48-hour sample (acuity-traffic-sample.csv) — timestamps are in UTC with fields: ts, rps_bucket, avg_tokens, streaming_flag. The sample shows two short spikes that align with what we described.

Hi Daniel / Tessa — I ran a first-pass sizing with the CSV you sent and sketched two options. Attached are the detail tables (latency-matrix.csv and warmpool-sizing.xlsx). Below are the assumptions and the math so everyone can validate quickly.

Quick assumptions (from sample + call):
- Full-fidelity model per-GPU concurrency (steady) = 40 concurrent infer requests (streaming reduces throughput by ~20% effective concurrency).
- Warm-up time for a cold GPU allocation = 75–110 seconds depending on model variant and container init.
- Average request token count (in sample) = 185 tokens; streaming calls average 8 tokens after first token.

Option A — Low-latency, higher-cost (aggressive warm pool):
- Prewarm: 30 GPUs in the region (30 * 40 = 1,200 concurrent slots).
- Expected p95 with warm pool: ~320 ms (streaming first-token < 100 ms).
- Cost: higher baseline given always-on GPUs, but near-zero scale-up risk.

Option B — Hybrid warm + fast autoscale (cost-conscious):
- Prewarm: 8 GPUs (capacity ~320 concurrent slots) + autoscale burst up to 40 GPUs when queue > 150 requests.
- Expected p95 under spikes < 450 ms for the first 45–90 seconds (depends on how many users hit streaming), then converge to ~340 ms once autoscale completes.
- Strategy: accept a short-lived degradation window (with fallback model as safety) vs. paying for full prewarm.

Queueing policy proposal:
- Short queue hold (<=5s) with priority for streaming calls. Streaming requests consume token-level slots; if queue > 5s, route new streaming calls to fallback model to preserve UX on full-fidelity call completions.

Fallback model suggestion:
- Small model with latency p95 ~120–150 ms and 0.2x cost — used for degraded reads only (15% of traffic). We’ll route non-critical/background inference to fallback in overload windows.

Requested confirmations from Acuity to finalize PoC config:
1) Are you comfortable with an initial PoC that uses Option B (hybrid) and the fallback model until we validate autoscale steady-state?
2) Any strict SLO gating that forbids sub-1-minute higher p95 during spikes?
3) Can you confirm the 15% fallback allowance in writing?

If we get confirmation, our next delivery is a detailed PoC plan (specific GPU SKU, prewarm orchestration script, test harness to replay your CSV) by Fri 10/23.

- Ben
